subject.title: fs-safe hardcoded 0o600 file mode ignores umask — breaks shared workspaces (NFS, SMB, multi-user)

question: Should unspecified fs-safe writes remain private by default, with shareable workspace artifacts opting into an explicit mode, or should the library-wide default become umask-respecting?
rationale: This is a cross-caller permission and security-contract choice; source-level repair cannot safely choose which artifacts may become group- or world-readable.

options.title: Keep the private library default
options.body: Require the owners of intentionally shared workspace artifacts to pass an explicit shareable mode and add focused coverage for `002` and restrictive umasks.

options.title: Adopt an umask-respecting library default
options.body: Change the library contract to request `0666` for unspecified writes and audit every caller that currently depends on private creation.

options.title: Add an operator policy surface
options.body: Expose a narrowly scoped shared-workspace policy only if explicit caller ownership cannot cover supported deployment needs without configuration.

recommendation.title: Keep the private library default
recommendation.body: Require the owners of intentionally shared workspace artifacts to pass an explicit shareable mode and add focused coverage for `002` and restrictive umasks.

likelyOwner.reason: The fs-safe package and its callers need a current feature-history owner identified before selecting a permanent permission policy.
